# GLASS: Generator for Large Scale Structure

## Overview

::: {layout-nrow="2"}

::: {.cell}

[GLASS](https://glass.readthedocs.io) is a code used in cosmology to generate
simulations of the full observable universe. In its current form, the primary
user base of the code are collaborations for large galaxy surveys, which are a
cornerstone of modern cosmology.

:::

::: {.cell}

![](figures/spheres.png){fig-alt="A three-part diagram of the GLASS code
simulation process. Left-to-right the diagram shows nested spherical shells of
the universe, a full-sky projection of cosmic matter density, and a
high-resolution zoomed-in view of density fluctuations."}

:::

## The Aim {footer=false}

1. Transform GLASS into a GPU-enabled code.
2. Improve the performance of simulations with GPU acceleration.
3. Implement and adapt parallel processing elements that utilise GPU
   capabilities.
4. Optimise GLASS for modern GPU architectures.
5. Enable differentiable simulations using JAX (in part or in full).
6. Embed GLASS within N-body simulations running on GPU infrastructure for
   post-processing.

# Python Array API Standard

# Our Experience

## Wrapping Functions Outside the Specification

```{.python code-line-numbers="|1-5|6|8-9|11-14"}
import numpy as np
from glass._types import AnyArray

def gradient(f: AnyArray) -> AnyArray:
    """Return the gradient of an N-dimensional array."""
    xp = f.__array_namespace__()

    if xp.__name__ in {"numpy", "jax.numpy"}:
        return xp.gradient(f)

    # If any other backend use default
    f_np = np.asarray(f, copy=True)
    result_np = np.gradient(f_np)
    return xp.asarray(result_np, copy=True)
```

## Handling the immutability of JAX {footer=false}

::: {.panel-tabset}

## NumPy

```{.python code-line-numbers="3|1|1,4-5|7-8|7-9|10|"}
import numpy as np

def yield_numpy_only_implementation(x):
    n = 10
    y = np.zeros((n, *x.shape))

    for i in range(n):
        for j, x_j in enumerate(x):
            y[i,...] = x_j * (i + j + 1)
        yield y
```

## Array API (JAX)

```{.python code-line-numbers="3|4|4-7|9-10|1,9-11|12-13|"}
import array_api_extra as xpx

def yield_array_api_compatible_implementation(x):
    xp = x.__array_namespace__()

    n = 10
    y = xp.zeros((n, *x.shape))

    for i in range(n):
        for j, x_j in enumerate(x):
            y = xpx.at(y)[i,...].set(x_j * (i + j + 1))
        # to avoid mutating in subsequent iterations
        yield xp.asarray(y, copy=True)
```

:::

## Benchmarking with `pytest-benchmark` {footer=false}

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Code Example

```{.python code-line-numbers="4-5|6,8-10|2,4,12|1,7,14|"}
import array_api_extra as xpx
import glass

def test_radialwindow(benchmark, xp) -> None:
    """check zeff is computed when not provided"""
    arr_length = 100_000
    expected_zeff = xp.asarray(66_666.0)

    wa = xp.arange(arr_length) # typos: ignore
    za = xp.arange(arr_length) # typos: ignore

    w = benchmark(glass.RadialWindow, za, wa)

    xpx.testing.assert_close(w.zeff, expected_zeff)
```

## Other

- No support for random number generation {{< fa brands github >}}
  [data-apis/array-api#874](https://github.com/data-apis/array-api/discussions/874).
- Typing is currently performed using unions of array typing awaiting
  {{< fa brands github >}}
  [data-apis/array-api-typing](https://github.com/data-apis/array-api-typing).

  ```{.python}
  from typing import TypeAlias
  import jaxtyping
  import numpy as np
  from array_api_strict._array_object import Array

  FloatArray: TypeAlias = (
      np.typing.NDArray[np.float64] | jaxtyping.Array | Array
  )
  ```

- Can contribute more functions to {{< fa brands github >}}
  [data-apis/array-api-extra](https://github.com/data-apis/array-api-extra).

# Conclusions

## {data-menu-title="Summary"}

- The Python Array API allows library maintainers to support multiple array
  backends.
- The framework is still new so only a few libraries have full support: `NumPy`,
  `JAX`, `CuPy`.
- Not all aspects of array backends are supported, e.g. random number
  generation, typing, …
- The standard comes with several packages to aid support:
  [`array-api-compat`](https://github.com/data-apis/array-api-compat),
  [`array-api-extra`](https://github.com/data-apis/array-api-extra),
  [`array-api-strict`](https://github.com/data-apis/array-api-strict),
  [`array-api-tests`](https://github.com/data-apis/array-api-tests),
  [`array-api-typing`](https://github.com/data-apis/array-api-typing).
- A route to GPU support and automatic differentiation.
